note: How a ship built in the ship builder becomes a carrier in the economy simulation. Everything here is a PLACEHOLDER ASSUMPTION unless marked canon: crew need and speed are derived from the ship (hold size, thrust-to-weight). The builder now has crew berths (cockpit 1, bunk 1, quarters 2; a hold needs one berth per crew) and a jump drive (+30% speed each, capped), but crew wages and ownership still come from this file.

cargo.note: The builder models cargo in tonnes per container, not volume. Volume is derived at a nominal 1,000 kg per SCU (grain and most bulk goods), so a 24 t hold is 24 SCU of space. Mass stays a separate hard limit, so dense goods hit the tonnage first and light goods hit the volume first (units.json: mass and volume are independent).

ownership.note: Insurance and financed share sit inside the canon ranges in economic_calibration.json (0.8-3.5% and 40-85%). Interest and depreciation are assumed.

speed.note: ly/day = reference * (empty thrust-to-weight / reference)^exponent, clamped. The starter ship (TWR 0.28) flies at the reference speed.

fuel.note: Tank tonnes x this = drive-feedstock units. A leg burns route.base_jump_fuel_units_per_mass_unit x ship mass (tonnes).
